text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The State Ownership Fund (FPS) has decided to sell off its 51 percent stake in fertiliser maker Azomures SA.
- Troubled Banca Dacia Felix SA will continue to have an interim manager until April when its shareholders gather at a general meeting.
ADEVARUL
- Fast-food giant McDonald's plans to increase its investment in Romania by $20 million this year, company manager Marian Alecu said.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Full privatisation is the most powerful incentive for foreign investors, a Bucharest broker says.
- Romania's government continues talks with international lenders on a reform and social package for Romania.
AZI
- Romania will increase its contribution to the capital of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development. Its contribution to the World Bank capital will remain unchanged.
LIBERTATEA
- Economic Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu plans to look into the FPS's privatisations so far to check whether company shares had been sold at undervalued prices.
CRONICA ROMANA
- The newspaper prints a two-page report on a recent round table conference it organised on the leu-dollar exchange rate and its implications in relaunching the Romanian economy.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania's accession to NATO is "a stake for stability in the area", the newspaper quotes French Socialist politician Michel Rocard as saying during a recent visit to Bucharest.

- Romanian police have made the first arrests in the case of post-communist inter-ethnic clashes during which Gypsy homes were burned down and the Gypsies were forced to flee their Transylvanian village of Hadareni.
ADEVARUL
- British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind is expected to arrive tonight for a 24-hour visit to Romania, the first by a British foreign minister since Douglas Hurd's 1993 visit.
- "The present government has no choice: either it implements genuine reforms, or it continues perestroika," the newspaper's editorial says, urging swift reforms to cure the economy.
ZIUA
- Seen from Sofia, Bucharest looks like the West, says a newspaper report on growing poverty that deepens the Bulgarian crisis.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- A two-page report outlines prosecutors' files on miners' union leader Miron Cosma's role in 1991 coalminer-led riots.
- The ex-ruling leftist Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) will ask president Emil Constantinescu to put an end to alleged "political purges" unleashed by the ruling centrists.
- Romania's strategic interests depend on the consolidation of neighbouring Ukraine's independence and statehood.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Hundreds of pensioners laid flowers at the grave of Romania's late Stalinist ruler Nicolae Ceausescu on Sunday to mark his birth anniversary.
- Constantinescu will meet opposition leaders at his Cotroceni palace on Tuesday and Wednesday.
CRONICA ROMANA

- Constantinescu has asked judges to brief him on progress in bringing to justice the owner of Romania's biggest pyramid investment scheme, which collapsed in 1994, taking with it the life savings of many Romanians.
